Notes: Andersen's āṇapayati cross-reference on printed p. 140 points to the following āṇapay- head, glossed 'to give an order, to command' and compared with Sanskrit ājñāpayati and Pali āṇāpeti. Turner 1096 ājñāpayati explicitly lists Ashokan āñapayāmi, aṇapemi, and ānapayisati. Andersen Ashokan command and causative verbs with printed variants

Andersen glosses ārādh- 'to please', causative 'to please, win favour', compares Sanskrit ārādhnoti and Pali ārādheti, and prints ārādhetave/ārodhetave/ārādhayitave. Turner 1316 ārādhayati lists Pali ārādheti and Ashokan aradheti, ārādhayaṁtu, ālādhayitu in the causative branch. Andersen Ashokan command and causative verbs with printed variants

Andersen's independently listed Rupnath ārodhetave says 'see ārādh-' and the preceding verb head identifies it as a Rupnath form of ārādhetave, dative infinitive causative. Turner 1316 supports the causative family. Andersen Ashokan command and causative verbs with printed variants

Andersen explicitly glosses the causative pavat- 'to practice [dhammaguna]', compares Sanskrit pra + √vart and Pali pavattati/pavatteti, and prints pavatitaviye/pavatitaviyā. Turner 8788 pravartayati, branch 3, gives Ashokan pavatayevū and pavatitaviyā 'to perform'. This is the verb, distinct from the following pavata- 'mountain'. Andersen Ashokan command and causative verbs with printed variants

Andersen's Rupnath pā line explicitly reads 'for pi, see pi'. The separate pi head is glossed 'also' and already links to Turner 485 ápi, whose article explicitly lists Ashokan pi. Andersen Ashokan command and causative verbs with printed variants
